I'm 65 this year, been working these 9 mu for 40 years. Didn't finish primary school, but I know this land better than any professor. There's seven of us in the house, but my two sons and their wives work in the factory in Handan, only come back for busy season. So day-to-day it's me, my wife, and my daughter-in-law, plus the kids after school. We farm 6 mu of wheat-maize double crop and 3 mu of cotton. Last year wheat did about 800 jin per mu, maize about 900 jin, cotton about 600 jin of seed cotton. Not a bad year.

This year I'll plant wheat around October 10th like always, using the improved variety from the seed station. Before planting I'll spread compound fertilizer — about one big bag per mu. Then in spring, if the wheat looks yellow at jointing, I'll topdress with half a bag of urea per mu. I irrigate three times: at planting if dry, at green-up, and at jointing. My neighbor Lao Wang did four times last year and got maybe 50 jin more, but the extra pumping cost him 25 yuan each time. I can't afford that.

For maize, soon as wheat comes off in early June, we plant. No time to plow — just plant right into the stubble. I buy hybrid seed every year, costs about 50 yuan per mu. One shot of fertilizer at planting, and I irrigate once or twice depending on the rains. Maize is easier than wheat.

Cotton I plant in late April. Needs herbicide and insecticide — bollworm is the big problem. I'll fertilize twice: base before planting and side-dress at flowering. Irrigate twice. The hard part is picking — takes many passes. I'm 65 now, my back aches, so I'll hire three days of labor at harvest. Costs money but I can't do it all myself.

All told, inputs will cost about 4,200 yuan this year. That's a big chunk. My son sent 5,000 yuan from town last month, so we'll manage. I don't try new tricks. I watch what my neighbors do, I remember what happened last year, and I don't take risks. Better to spend a bit more on fertilizer and sleep easy than save a few yuan and lose the crop.
